observations.statement: The excerpt establishes deterministic Instruction, Work, and Memory bundle ordering and makes Work Bundle acceptance criteria nontruncatable.
Model-switch re-packing preserves recent material, summarizes older turns, applies capacity-driven removal, normalizes provider formatting, and runs synchronously.

Assistant memory and project retrieval are distinct injection classes; the excerpt gives Assistant memory an explicit Verified-only eligibility gate while project retrieval is fresh Work Bundle material controlled by allowlists, budgets, and Context Lens.
Context Lens changes effective context through immediate Mute and Focus toggles or an applied Subcompact artifact, and its shaping participates in child handoff construction.
BrainStorm execution crosses an explicit read-only-to-write authority boundary by switching chat from Plan mode to Agent mode, after which either the manager or user selects an execution topology.
HITL gates are exposed through both Dashboard and Assistant channels, create a dedicated thread, and allow natural-language or direct-control approval.
Dev sessions have visible lifecycle states, can span several terminal identities, preserve historical evidence after stopping, and remain represented when the user changes projects.
The gap section combines blanket MVP-closure language with an explicit feature marked absent from this plan and a later statement disclaiming blanket closure.

candidate_findings.title: Context Lens can bypass the acceptance-criteria preservation invariant
candidate_findings.claim: The excerpt prohibits truncating Work Bundle acceptance criteria, but Mute may exclude selected messages and Subcompact may replace a selected region with a summary. It provides no protected-content carve-out or precedence rule preventing either operation from removing or lossily rewriting acceptance criteria.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: An agent could execute against altered acceptance conditions without the event technically being classified as truncation, defeating the stated invariant and making context behavior nonconformant but difficult to detect.

candidate_findings.title: Model re-pack has contradictory preservation semantics and no impossible-fit state
candidate_findings.negative_space_dimension: failure and recovery, scale, and test oracles
candidate_findings.claim: The procedure says the last six turns are preserved unconditionally and later says oldest preserved turns are dropped. It also does not define what happens when the system prompt plus other protected material and Work Bundle acceptance criteria alone exceed the effective window.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A conforming implementation cannot satisfy both directives in an over-capacity case and must invent whether to reject the run, switch models, omit material, or violate a protected-content invariant.

candidate_findings.title: Context budgeting lacks a cross-provider calculation and normalization oracle
candidate_findings.claim: Injector budgets are expressed as bytes, lines, and headings while model fit is expressed through several token-capacity fields. The excerpt does not define tokenization, which capacity field governs, reserved space for output and tool schemas, or the failure result when provider-specific content cannot be normalized.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: The same context can fit on one provider and overflow on another, and independent implementations can produce different truncation decisions while all claiming compliance.

candidate_findings.title: Mandatory Assistant-memory calls have no availability or recovery contract
candidate_findings.negative_space_dimension: failure and recovery, operations, and states
candidate_findings.claim: Every selected-project Assistant turn must call two memory interfaces, but the excerpt does not specify timeouts, cancellation, unavailable-service behavior, partial-result handling, stale-capsule handling, retry limits, or whether a turn may proceed without memory.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A memory subsystem fault can either block all project chat turns or cause implementations to silently omit required context, with no common user-visible or machine-testable outcome.

candidate_findings.title: Project retrieval has no trust boundary equivalent to memory eligibility gating
candidate_findings.claim: Assistant memory has an explicit Verified-only default, but retrieved chat, code, and logs enter the Work Bundle with only allowlist, mode, budget, and Lens controls. The excerpt supplies no provenance requirement, hostile-instruction treatment, data-versus-instruction boundary, secret filtering, or trust classification for retrieved material.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Untrusted repository text or logs can influence an executing agent as Work Bundle context or expose sensitive material even though the adjacent memory path is verification-gated.

candidate_findings.title: Default-On Auto Retrieval has no required effective-state disclosure
candidate_findings.negative_space_dimension: misleading GUI truth and test oracles
candidate_findings.claim: Project retrieval remains optional with MAY semantics while its thread chip defaults to On. The required Injected Context breakdown does not require reporting whether retrieval was attempted, skipped, failed, returned no results, or contributed content.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: The GUI can display On while no retrieval occurred, leaving users unable to distinguish a legitimate empty result from a disabled, failed, or ignored retrieval path.

candidate_findings.title: Immediate Context Lens changes lack an in-flight snapshot boundary
candidate_findings.negative_space_dimension: states, transitions, propagation, and misleading GUI truth
candidate_findings.claim: Mute and Focus apply immediately, but the excerpt does not define whether a toggle affects a prompt already assembling, a request already dispatched, only the next turn, or child handoffs created concurrently. No context revision, acknowledgement, or persistence boundary is required.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: The visible selection and the context actually used by an agent or child can diverge nondeterministically, especially during streaming, retries, and concurrent handoff construction.

candidate_findings.title: Subcompact artifact authority and recovery are unspecified
candidate_findings.negative_space_dimension: authority, failure and recovery, and compatibility
candidate_findings.claim: Subcompact creates a local summary artifact that replaces source messages, but the excerpt does not identify the summary producer, model or algorithm version, provenance fields, validation rule, invalidation after source edits, cancellation behavior, atomic commit point, or recovery from partial creation.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A stale, failed, or provider-dependent summary can silently become effective context despite preserved source history, and rehydration handles alone do not establish that the replacement is trustworthy or current.

candidate_findings.title: BrainStorm execution crosses into write authority without a complete transition contract
candidate_findings.claim: The phrase “starts or executes” causes a switch from read-only Plan mode to write/execute Agent mode, but the excerpt does not define the qualifying user action, confirmation and approval checks, permission-profile propagation, frozen plan revision, executor-selection disclosure, or rollback if the switch or dispatch fails.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: An ambiguous UI action can become an authority escalation or execute a different plan revision or topology than the user intended.

candidate_findings.title: HITL approval is not bound to an immutable gate target
candidate_findings.negative_space_dimension: authority, security, and failure and recovery
candidate_findings.claim: The excerpt accepts natural-language “approve and continue” and an optional direct Dashboard control across several gate types, but does not require a run ID, gate ID, gate revision, authorized actor, current-state check, confirmation payload, stale-action rejection, or idempotency key.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: With multiple or replayed CtAs, an approval can target the wrong or obsolete gate, be processed twice, or resume side-effecting work after the underlying state changed. That defeats the safety purpose of mandatory approval gates.

candidate_findings.title: Dedicated HITL thread creation lacks deduplication and lifecycle rules
candidate_findings.claim: A new thread is spawned when the orchestrator pauses, but the excerpt does not define event replay deduplication, reuse for an existing gate thread, naming collision handling, behavior when the Assistant is busy, supersession, resolution marking, archival, or cleanup.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Retries and reconnects can create duplicate approval threads and notifications whose CtAs disagree about which gate remains actionable.

candidate_findings.title: Continue in Assistant uses an unbounded and unauditable context handoff
candidate_findings.negative_space_dimension: propagation, security and privacy, and misleading GUI truth
candidate_findings.claim: The handoff injects loosely described “relevant context,” may create or select a thread, and may add a suggested prompt, but has no required schema, provenance, source revision, target-selection rule, redaction policy, size budget, deduplication behavior, or failure state.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: The action can leak run data into the wrong thread, omit decisive gate facts, duplicate stale context, or make a natural-language approval appear grounded when its summary is incomplete or outdated.

candidate_findings.title: Dev actions lack immutable project and session binding across project switches
candidate_findings.claim: Switching projects recalculates effective shell and dev state while old-project sessions remain visible, and reveal actions operate on a current dev_session_id. The excerpt does not require every command to carry and validate both project identity and session identity or reject stale cross-project UI actions.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A delayed click, shortcut, or Assistant command can stop, reveal, or otherwise affect a background session belonging to the previous project.

candidate_findings.title: Active dev-session close consequences have no complete state machine
candidate_findings.negative_space_dimension: states, transitions, and failure and recovery
candidate_findings.claim: Close must disclose consequences and must not silently orphan work “by default,” but the excerpt does not enumerate cancel, stop, detach, transfer, or keep-running outcomes; their defaults and postconditions; or forced-close, crash, timeout, and partial-stop recovery.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Different surfaces can apply incompatible close behavior, lose ownership references, or leave live processes that the UI can no longer control.

candidate_findings.title: Preserved shell evidence has no retention or privacy lifecycle
candidate_findings.negative_space_dimension: security and privacy, operations, and scale
candidate_findings.claim: Stopping a dev session preserves historical shell evidence and linked surface history, but the excerpt provides no retention limit, redaction rule, access control, storage quota, deletion operation, or treatment of credentials and other sensitive terminal output.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Long-lived terminal history can accumulate secrets and unbounded data after process exit, with no specified way to expire or securely remove it.

candidate_findings.title: MVP closure and traceability claims are internally non-auditable
candidate_findings.negative_space_dimension: governance, misleading truth, and test oracles
candidate_findings.claim: The section says all gaps below are adopted and that all listed features are in scope, yet its comparison marks Agent skills as not in this plan and its traceability prose later says it does not claim blanket closure. The excerpt provides no finding-to-owner-to-acceptance-test mapping that resolves those statements.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Readiness tooling or implementers can treat an open or externally owned feature as closed, while reviewers have no deterministic trace for deciding which closure statement governs.

candidate_findings.title: Concurrent-thread limits omit admission control and backpressure semantics
candidate_findings.claim: The excerpt distinguishes a default Assistant limit of 10 from a global limit of 32 and says the more restrictive limit wins, but does not define scheduling, queuing, fairness, resource reservations, rejection UX, starvation prevention, or what happens to running and queued work when either limit decreases.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Two conforming schedulers can behave incompatibly, and a ten-thread burst can exhaust provider, terminal, or memory resources without a predictable user-visible state.

candidate_findings.title: The no-project state has no capability matrix or transition behavior
candidate_findings.negative_space_dimension: missing callers, states, and test oracles
candidate_findings.claim: The excerpt says “many chat features” do not work without a selected project but does not enumerate enabled, disabled, hidden, or degraded features; required error copy; treatment of an in-flight turn when its project is deselected; or clearing of project-derived context.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: The UI and runtime can disagree about whether memory, retrieval, file references, tools, dev sessions, and commands remain available, creating context leakage and untestable disabled-state behavior.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: Multi-question clarification identity and deterministic resume are explicitly required through canonical question IDs and restoration of the outstanding or resolved questionnaire state.
Chat is explicitly prohibited from inventing parallel dev-output, account-routing, or approval-mode ownership.
Assistant memory is explicitly barred from subagent and non-Assistant execution paths.
The chat-facing dev lifecycle explicitly includes starting, active, failed, stopping, stopped, and restored-historical states, and output remains owned by canonical shell surfaces.
Old-project background activity must remain visible after switching projects, and closing an active dev-session tab requires consequence disclosure rather than silent orphaning by default.
Accessibility is explicitly excluded from MVP for the per-thread plan-panel requirement, so its absence is not treated here as an accidental MVP omission.
The adopted chat error path explicitly names Resend and Cancel and says the queue remains unchanged unless the user resends.
Assistant thread concurrency and global runtime-agent concurrency are explicitly distinguished, with the more restrictive applicable limit taking precedence.

exact_evidence_refs.excerpt: Rule: For every Assistant turn (and any chat-triggered run), the context pipeline MUST assemble the run context as three explicit bundles, in this deterministic order: (1) Instruction Bundle, (2) Work Bundle, (3) Memory Bundle.

Rule: The Work Bundle acceptance criteria MUST NEVER be truncated; if truncation is required to fit a model’s window, truncation MUST occur in instruction example/illustrative content first and in conversation summaries/older turns before any acceptance criteria content is removed.

Rule: The chat UI MUST surface an “Injected Context” breakdown per run/turn, including: included `AGENTS.md` paths + byte counts; parent summary and attempt journal inclusion + byte counts; and whether truncation occurred (and the reason/order that was applied).

Rule: The three context injectors MUST be user-configurable (per-project; optional per-run override) with deterministic defaults; budget defaults (bytes/lines/headings) MUST be decided deterministically and recorded via `auto_decisions.jsonl`.

1. **Preserve unconditionally:** System prompt, Instruction Bundle (`AGENTS.md` chain where enabled), active file references, last 6 turns verbatim (config: `context.repack.verbatim_turns`, default `6`).
2. **Summarize:** All turns older than the last 6 are condensed into a single "Conversation Summary" block (key decisions, file paths mentioned, outcomes).
3. **Truncate:** If the preserved + summarized content exceeds the new model's effective context window from the Models_System capability snapshot, truncate the summary first, then drop oldest preserved turns until it fits. Never truncate the system prompt or the Work Bundle acceptance criteria.
4. **Normalize:** Provider-specific formatting (e.g., tool call syntax) is normalized to the new provider's expected format.
5. **Timing:** Re-pack runs synchronously before the next turn is sent. The user sees a brief "Repacking context…" indicator.

Config: `context.repack.verbatim_turns` (default `6`). Max tokens are sourced from the selected provider/model capability snapshot fields owned by `Plans/Models_System.md`, including `context_window_tokens`, `max_input_tokens`, and `effective_context_window_tokens`.

Rule: For Assistant turns with a selected project, chat context assembly MUST call the Assistant-memory SSOT interfaces (`build_capsule(project_id, now)` and `search(project_id, user_message, now, k)`) and MUST enforce the configured capsule/retrieval budgets.
Rule: Automatic memory injection in chat MUST apply eligibility gating per the Assistant-memory SSOT (Verified-only by default; any Unverified inclusion requires explicit user action).
Rule: Assistant memory MUST NOT be forwarded to subagents or non-Assistant execution paths from chat.

In addition to the Assistant-only memory capsule (§17.4), the chat context pipeline MAY inject **project-scoped retrieved context** (chat/code/logs) per §10.1. This is designed to keep long-running threads usable without relying on full-history in-context.

Rule: Project retrieval injection MUST remain **separate** from Assistant memory injection:
- Project retrieval injection is **fresh, ephemeral context for the current turn** (Work Bundle: “Retrieved Context”).
- Assistant memory injection remains governed by verification + gist rules (Plans/assistant-memory-subsystem.md) and is never implicitly expanded by chat/code/log retrieval.

Rule: Project retrieval injection MUST respect:
- **Thread-local Auto Retrieval override** (chip; default On; user can disable per thread).
- **Per-project retrieval settings** (allowlist + modes + budgets; Settings/Memory).
- **Context Lens overlays** (§17.6) to avoid injecting muted content or ignoring focused selections.

Mode behavior:
- all three modes support selecting multiple messages at once.
- `Mute` applies immediately as selection toggles happen.
- `Focus` applies immediately as selection toggles happen.
- `Subcompact` prepares a selection and then requires an explicit apply action because it creates a local summary artifact.
- `Turn Off` exits Context Lens mode and clears the active selection state.

Context assembly rules:
- muted messages are excluded from effective context assembly and from chatsearch results returned to the agent.
- focused messages remain protected and high-priority in effective context assembly.
- Subcompact replaces the selected message region in effective context assembly with a local summary while preserving canonical source history and rehydration handles.
- Context Lens state is thread-local UI shaping, not Assistant memory.
- child handoff bundles derive from canonical source state plus current effective shaping state; children do not inherit a lossy copy as their only truth.

- **Execution:** When the user **starts or executes** the plan, the **chat must switch to Agent mode** (execution mode), because Plan mode is read-only and execution requires write/execute permissions.
- **Who executes:** The plan can be executed by:
  - A **regular agent**,
  - A **crew**, or
  - **Agent + subagents**.
  The **manager** (orchestrator) automatically decides, or the **user can request** which option.

The **Dashboard** displays **warnings** and **Calls to Action (CtAs)** that require or benefit from user attention. These are not only informational: the user is expected to **answer or address** them.

- **Warnings:** e.g. approaching usage limits, config wiring gaps, Doctor findings, or run state that needs review. Shown on the Dashboard so the user sees them without opening another view.
- **Calls to Action (CtAs):** Items that need an explicit user action -- e.g. approve, acknowledge, run a suggested action, or fix a configuration issue. CtAs prompt the user to interact.

**Addressable via the chat Assistant:** Warnings and CtAs can be **answered or addressed by the chat Assistant**. The user can:
- Open the Assistant and respond in natural language (e.g. "approve and continue," "what's blocking?", "run the suggested fix").
- Use the Assistant to discuss or clarify before taking action (e.g. "summarize what was done in this phase" before approving a HITL gate).

**HITL prompts:** When Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) is enabled and the orchestrator pauses on a blocked-runtime, package-complete, seam-complete, or mandatory side-effect approval gate:
  - The **Dashboard** shows a **CtA** that prompts the user to interact (e.g. "Package gate complete -- approval required to continue").
  - A **new thread** is **spawned** with an **appropriate name** (e.g. tied to the package/seam/node or "Approval: Package Gate") so the user has a dedicated place to respond. That thread shows the CtA; the user can address it there via the Assistant (e.g. "approve and continue" or ask for a summary and then approve). So the user is notified on the Dashboard and in a dedicated HITL thread.
  The user can also address the CtA via the Assistant in that thread (e.g. "approve and continue" or ask for a summary and then approve) or via a direct "Approve & continue" control on the Dashboard if provided. See **Plans/human-in-the-loop.md** for HITL settings (GUI) and behavior.

**Orchestrator to Assistant handoff:** When the orchestrator **completes** a run or **pauses** (e.g. at a blocked episode, package/seam gate, or run-completion review point), the Dashboard/completion UI must offer the canonical CtA **Continue in Assistant**. That action opens the Assistant chat with **relevant context** injected: e.g. run summary, current package/seam/node/blocked episode id, and a short summary of what was done. The user can then continue in natural language ("approve and continue", "what should we do next?") without re-pasting. Implementation: Dashboard CtA or completion panel includes a control that switches to Assistant view, creates or selects a thread, and injects a context block (run summary, package/seam/node, optional suggested prompt).

Rules:
- assistant-invoked dev actions map to stable UI commands and visible shell state changes
- `start hot reload dev mode`, `start dev server`, and `run tests in watch mode` are user-facing intents that resolve to canonical `cmd.dev.*` or terminal command IDs
- the chat surface shows whether a dev session is starting, active, failed, stopping, stopped, or restored as historical state
- output routes into the canonical Terminal, Output, Problems, Debug Console, and Ports surfaces owned by the shell; chat does not create a parallel dev-output model
- project switch or workspace-tab close must surface explicit consequences for any active dev session

Rules:
- a dev session may span multiple workgroups, leaf panes, and editor-embedded terminal panels.
- `Show Output`, `Show Problems`, and `Show Ports` reveal the surfaces linked to the current `dev_session_id` without changing the canonical owning runtime records.
- `Open in Terminal` from a dev-status row reveals the primary or last-active terminal leaf pane for that dev session when one exists.
- closing a workgroup or pane that is mirrored in the editor stack must remove or update the associated editor panel references.
- if a pane exists only in the editor stack, the bottom workspace surfaces placeholder guidance rather than pretending the pane no longer exists.
- stopping a dev session preserves historical shell evidence and linked surface history even when the live process has exited.

### Project-switch and close rules
- switching projects recalculates effective shell, tool, and dev-session state for the new project context
- background activity from the old project remains visible through badges and attention surfaces tied to its own project and session identities
- closing a workspace tab or terminal tab with an active dev session requires explicit consequence disclosure; Puppet Master MUST NOT silently orphan the background workflow by default

This section reviews the Assistant & Chat plan for **gaps**, **potential problems**, and **competitive coverage** (vs. OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Antigravity, Cursor). **All gaps listed below are adopted as MVP:** the main body of this plan (§1-§22) has been updated to include every adopted requirement (slash commands, interrupt vs. stop, up to 2 queued messages FIFO, Plan read-only until execute, thinking toggle, export, compact, model switch UI, resume/rewind, revert last edit, session share, HITL dashboard + thread notification).
| **Agent skills (load by trigger)** | -- | Skills/hooks | -- | ✅ Agent Skills | -- | -- | ⚠️ newfeatures §6; not in this plan |

**Summary:** All listed features are now in scope: steer/queue (§4), context display (§12), permissions (§3), MCP (§7), @ mention (§9), **LSP-aware chat/editor integration (§9, Plans/LSPSupport.md §5)**, activity transparency (§13), multi-agent (§14-§15), slash commands (§5), export (§6), thinking toggle (§13), model switch (§1), user compact (§17), resume/rewind (§11), revert edit (§9), session share (§11). **LSP is MVP** (editor + Chat). Inbox-per-agent and real-time collaboration are out of scope for the initial desktop MVP (see glossary in table above).
12. **No project selected** -- §1: many chat features do not work when no project is selected; only application rules apply.

22. **Concurrent threads** -- §11: user-facing setting, **default 10** max concurrent thread runs in Assistant UI. This is a thread-level Assistant concurrency setting, not the global runtime subagent ceiling. Global orchestration caps remain SSOT in `Plans/orchestrator-subagent-integration.md` and `Plans/Run_Modes.md` (`max_total_active_agents=32`), and interview reviewer narrowing remains in `Plans/interview-subagent-integration.md`; the more restrictive applicable limit wins.
    - Copy and deep-link labels may use `context-detail` and `concurrent-thread` only as Assistant UI route/copy tokens; they must continue to reflect this owner section and must not redefine global runtime concurrency.
24. **Plan panel scope** -- §11: plan panel **per thread**. **Accessibility** is **not MVP**.
25. **Error and failure UX** -- §4: clear error state, Resend or Cancel, queue unchanged unless user resends; suggest switch platform or model when appropriate.
